ai_summary: The Cellular Jail (Kala Pani), built by the British between 1896 and 1906, was the colonial prison used to exile political prisoners to the Andamans; freedom fighters including Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, Batukeshwar Dutt and Yogendra Shukla were incarcerated here. Today it is a national memorial with preserved cells, a gallery of the freedom movement, and an evening light-and-sound show narrating its history. Located in Sri Vijaya Puram (formerly Port Blair) near the harbour.
place_tip: Attend the evening light-and-sound show for the full story; buy show tickets early as evening slots sell out in peak season.
cost: Rs 30
address: Rajiv Gandhi Rd, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

place_name: Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island)
name_english: Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island)
ai_summary: Ross Island, renamed Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep in 2018, was the administrative headquarters of the British in the Andamans, once called the 'Paris of the East'. Today its colonial buildings - church, printing press, Chief Commissioner's house - stand in jungle-clad ruins, home to wild spotted deer. Reached by a 10-15 minute ferry from Aberdeen Jetty / Rajiv Gandhi Water Sports Complex in Port Blair (now Sri Vijaya Puram).
place_tip: Combine Ross Island with North Bay Island on one ferry ticket; carry photo ID - it is mandatory for bookings and transfers.
cost: Rs 470 (round-trip ferry); island entry ~Rs 30
address: Ross Island, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744104 (ferry from Aberdeen Jetty)

ai_summary: North Bay Island is the water-sports hub near Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), known for coral reefs, snorkeling, glass-bottom boat rides, sea walking and scuba diving. There is no island entry fee; costs are for the ferry from the Rajiv Gandhi Water Sports Complex and the activities. Ferries to North Bay typically leave in the morning and return by mid-afternoon.
place_tip: Book on the first morning boat to avoid crowds; buy activity tickets from official counters and carry cash - digital payments may not work on the island.
cost: Rs 0 (island); round-trip boat ~Rs 870 with Ross Island
address: North Bay Island, off Sri Vijaya Puram (boat from Rajiv Gandhi Water Sports Complex)

ai_summary: Corbyn's Cove is the closest beach to Sri Vijaya Puram (formerly Port Blair), about 7-9 km from the city centre, lined with coconut palms on a crescent shoreline. It offers swimming in shallow areas, jet skiing, parasailing and sea karting, plus food stalls and souvenir shops. Entry to the beach is free; water sports and parking are charged.
place_tip: Go in the late afternoon for the best light and sunset; swim only in shallow areas and heed lifeguards - currents can be strong beyond the shallows.
cost: Rs 0
address: Corbyn's Cove, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

ai_summary: Samudrika, run by the Indian Navy near Haddo in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), documents the Andaman and Nicobar Islands under history, geography, people, marine life and archaeology. Highlights include a blue-whale skeleton, coral and shell collections, and exhibits on the islands' tribes and naval heritage. 'Samudrika' derives from 'Samudra', meaning sea.
place_tip: Avoid Mondays - the museum is closed; combine with the nearby Cellular Jail and Anthropological Museum for a half-day museum circuit.
cost: Rs 50
address: Haddo Road, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744102

ai_summary: The Zonal Anthropological Museum in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), maintained by the Anthropological Survey of India, exhibits the life and culture of the islands' six indigenous tribes - Onges, Jarawas, Sentinelese, Great Andamanese, Shompens and Nicobarese - through tools, weapons, canoes, ornaments and photographs. Established in 1975, it is a compact 1-hour visit near Phoenix Bay on MG Road.
place_tip: Photography and videography are generally not permitted inside; arrive at least 90 minutes before closing and carry a photo ID.
cost: Rs 10
address: MG Road, Phoenix Bay, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

ai_summary: Chatham Saw Mill, on Chatham Island connected to Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) by a 100-metre bridge, began operations in 1883 and is described as Asia's oldest and largest continuously operational sawmill. Run by the Forest Department, it processes prized Andaman timber such as padauk and houses a Forest Museum plus World War II bomb craters from Japanese bombing.
place_tip: Go in the morning - the mill only admits visitors in the first half of the day; it is an active industrial site so expect noise.
cost: Rs 10
address: Chatham Island, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744102

place_name: Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park (Wandoor / Jolly Buoy)
name_english: Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park (Wandoor / Jolly Buoy)
ai_summary: Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park, ~25-30 km south of Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) at Wandoor, is a 281 sq km marine protected area of 15 islands. Only Jolly Buoy and Red Skin islands are open to tourists, offering glass-bottom boat rides, snorkeling and pristine beaches over live coral. Permits are limited (about 150 per day, first-come) and collected at Wandoor Jetty; it is a no-plastic zone.
place_tip: Reach Wandoor Jetty by 8:15 AM for the 9 AM boats - permits are first-come first-served and run out in peak season; carry packed lunch, nothing is available on the island.
cost: Rs 50 (entry); boat Rs 650 per person (Jolly Buoy)
address: Wandoor Jetty, Sri Vijaya Puram tehsil, South Andaman 744301

ai_summary: Chidiya Tapu, about 25 km south of Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) at the southern tip of South Andaman, is the islands' best-known sunset point, with mangrove forests, rich birdlife and the Munda Pahad trek. The beach and sunset point are free; swimming is not advised due to rocky shores and saltwater crocodile warnings. The nearby Chidiya Tapu Biological Park is ticketed.
place_tip: Arrive by 4 PM for a good sunset spot; pre-book return transport - there is no public transport back after dark and the road is poorly lit.
cost: Rs 0 (beach); Biological Park ~Rs 20
address: Chidiya Tapu, South Andaman, Sri Vijaya Puram 744105

ai_summary: The Fisheries Museum near the Rajiv Gandhi Water Sports Complex in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) displays marine species, corals and shells of the Andaman and Nicobar waters, with small aquarium tanks. It is a compact, educational half-hour stop popular with families and students, and is one of the cheapest ticketed attractions in town.
place_tip: Pair it with the Water Sports Complex and Marina Park in one visit; note it is closed on Mondays and second Saturdays.
cost: Rs 5
address: Near Rajiv Gandhi Water Sports Complex, Sri Vijaya Puram 744104

ai_summary: Aberdeen Bazaar is the main commercial market street of Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), the island capital's shopping heart for clothes, electronics, groceries and local snacks. It is also the transport hub - the central bus stand at Mohanpura and the Aberdeen Jetty for island ferries are nearby. A practical stop for supplies between sightseeing.
place_tip: Shop in the evening when the market is liveliest; fix auto-rickshaw fares before boarding - there are no meters.
address: Aberdeen Bazaar, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

ai_summary: Sagarika is the government-run handicrafts emporium (ANIHDC) on MG Road in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), selling authentic Andamanese handicrafts at fixed prices - shell ornaments, coconut-shell lamps, padauk wood carvings, cane and bamboo work, and Nicobari beadwork. It is the reliable spot for genuine souvenirs supporting local artisans.
place_tip: Prices are fixed and fair - no bargaining needed; visit in the morning for a quieter browse.
cost: Rs 0
address: MG Road, DAG Colony, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

ai_summary: The Rajiv Gandhi Water Sports Complex at Marina Park in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) is the city's waterfront promenade and water-sports hub, named after the former PM who visited in 1987. It hosts jet skiing, parasailing, banana rides, snorkeling, scuba diving, sea walking and glass-bottom boats, plus a children's park, cafeteria and souvenir shops. Entry to the complex is free; activities are ticketed.
place_tip: Do water activities in the morning (8 AM-12 PM) when the sea is calmest; buy tickets only from official counters for proper receipts and refunds.
cost: Rs 0
address: Marina Park Road, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

ai_summary: Flag Point, on the road to Corbyn's Cove Beach, marks the historic spot where Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose hoisted the national flag on December 30, 1943, declaring the Andaman and Nicobar Islands the first liberated territory of India. A giant 150-foot Tricolour now flies here, dedicated in 2018. It is an open public viewpoint with sea views, liveliest in the evening.
place_tip: Visit in the evening for sunset photos with the giant Tricolour; it pairs well as a stop on the way to Corbyn's Cove Beach.
address: Corbyn's Cove Road, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

ai_summary: Jogger's Park at AHW Colony, Shadipur, is a popular public fitness park in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) with jogging tracks, open lawns and panoramic views of the airport and harbour. Locals use it for morning runs, yoga and evening walks; tourists visit for sunrise and sunset views and plane-spotting. Entry is free.
place_tip: Go at sunrise for the best views and local atmosphere; photographing the airport runway itself is not permitted.
cost: Rs 0
address: AHW Colony, Shadipur, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

ai_summary: World War II-era Japanese bunkers stand along the Corbyn's Cove Beach area in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), remnants of the Japanese occupation of the Andamans from March 1942 to October 1945. The concrete pillboxes and gun emplacements, set among the palms near the beach, are a quiet heritage stop for history buffs visiting Corbyn's Cove.
place_tip: Combine with a Corbyn's Cove beach visit; the bunkers are easy to miss - ask a local or auto driver for the exact spot.
cost: Rs 0
address: Near Corbyn's Cove Beach, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

ai_summary: Viper Island, a 20-minute boat ride from Phoenix Bay Jetty in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), was the site of the old British jail before the Cellular Jail was built, with a hilltop gallows used for executions. Named after the vessel HMS Viper that brought Lt. Archibald Blair to the Andamans in 1789, its ruins are now a quiet picnic and heritage spot. There is no entry fee; the only cost is the boat fare.
place_tip: Visit in the morning to avoid the harsh afternoon sun; carry water and sun protection - there are no eateries on the island.
cost: Rs 75 (ferry; island free)
address: Viper Island, off Phoenix Bay Jetty, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands

name_english: Mount Harriet National Park (now Mount Manipur)
ai_summary: Mount Harriet, the highest point in South Andaman and now officially Mount Manipur, offers panoramic views of Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), Ross Island and Havelock from its viewpoint. Reached via ferry from Chatham Jetty to Bamboo Flat and a road climb, the park has nature trails, watchtowers and the Kala Pathar viewpoint. It is about 55 km by road or 15 km by sea from the city.
place_tip: Take the morning ferry from Chatham Jetty to Bamboo Flat (~15 min), then a taxi up; start early and plan to be back down by late afternoon.
cost: Rs 25
address: Hope Town / Bamboo Flat side, Sri Vijaya Puram, South Andaman 744107

ai_summary: Baratang Island, about 100 km north of Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) by the Andaman Trunk Road, is the classic full-day trip for the limestone caves - stalactite and stalagmite formations reached by speedboat through mangrove creeks - and the mud volcano, described as India's only active one. The road convoy passes through the Jarawa Tribal Reserve, where stopping and photography are strictly prohibited. Permits are handled by tour operators; Indians need only photo ID.
place_tip: Start before dawn (3:30-4 AM) to catch the first convoy at Jirkatang; carry a small torch for the caves and do not photograph anything inside the tribal reserve.
cost: Rs 900 (speedboat to Limestone Caves)
address: Nilambur Jetty / Baratang, Middle Andaman, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744201

ai_summary: Kalapani Museum at Garacharma II in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) is a private museum showcasing the history of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands through dioramas, photographs and films, including archival material on the Japanese occupation of 1942-1945. Ticketed entry includes a guide, photography charges and tea or coffee. It is open seven days a week, 9 AM to 7 PM.
place_tip: Call ahead to confirm it is open on your day; the entry fee includes a guided tour, so take it - it adds a lot of context.
address: Garacharma II, ATR, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands

ai_summary: New Lighthouse Restaurant at Marina Park near the Rajiv Gandhi Water Sports Complex in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) is a long-running seafood spot known for its daily-catch dishes like red snapper tawa fry and Chinese-style lobster. Reviews note knowledgeable waiters who help pick from the fresh catch; cash or UPI payments only.
place_tip: Ask the waiter for the day's fresh catch recommendation - that is the strength of the place; carry cash/UPI as cards are not accepted.
address: Marina Park, Rajiv Gandhi Nagar, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744104

ai_summary: Amaya is the rooftop restaurant and bar at SeaShell Hotel on Marine Hill in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), known for live barbecued and grilled seafood, fusion of international and Indian cuisines, live music and city-wide views. It is one of the top-rated evening spots in town, with standouts like garlic lobster and sizzlers.
place_tip: Go for dinner to get the rooftop views with live music; reserve on weekends and dry days - it is a popular evening venue.
address: SeaShell Hotel, Marine Hill, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744104

ai_summary: Annapurna Cafeteria Pure Veg, opposite Model School on MA Road at Aberdeen Bazaar in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), is the town's best-known pure-vegetarian restaurant, serving dosas, idlis, vadas, thalis, North Indian curries and Chinese options. Budget-friendly and open daily 7 AM to 10 PM, it is a local favourite for breakfast and casual family meals.
place_tip: Try the masala dosa breakfast or a veg thali (around Rs 250-400); it gets crowded at peak hours, so go slightly off-peak.
address: 71, MA Rd, opp. Model School, Aberdeen Bazaar, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

ai_summary: Adi Bengali Hotel on MA Road at Phoenix Bay in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) is a no-frills Bengali eatery serving home-style fish curry, rice and Bengali meals. A favourite with locals and budget travellers, it is the place for an authentic, cheap Bengali lunch near the Phoenix Bay jetty area.
place_tip: Order the fish curry with rice - the Bengali preparation is the draw; expect simple, canteen-style seating.
address: 60, MA Rd, Phoenix Bay, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

ai_summary: Mandalay Restaurant, inside the Fortune Resort Bay on Marine Hill in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), serves Indian, Asian and Chinese fare including a popular buffet drawing both Indian and foreign tourists. Reviewers praise the spicy chicken curry, Chinese stir-fried vegetables and dragon fruit juice; it does not serve alcohol.
place_tip: Go for the buffet if you want variety - the spread suits families and groups; confirm current buffet availability when booking.
address: Fortune Resort Bay, Marine Hill, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

ai_summary: Sea Food Delights is a rooftop seafood restaurant on MA Road in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) offering grilled whole fish, fish curry, crispy prawns and other seafood with a panoramic sea view. Moderately priced and popular for dinner, it is a solid alternative to the Marina Park seafood spots.
place_tip: Book an evening table for the rooftop sea view; confirm the day's specials with the staff before ordering.
address: MA Rd, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands

ai_summary: Radhanagar Beach, locally known as Beach No. 7, is the flagship beach of Swaraj Dweep (formerly Havelock Island) on the island's western coast, about 12 km from Havelock Jetty. It was named 'Best Beach in Asia' by Time magazine in 2004 and holds Blue Flag certification for cleanliness, safety and environmental management. No motorised water sports are allowed, so the beach stays calm and quiet, and it is famous for its long stretch of powdery white sand, turquoise water and sunsets.
place_tip: Reach by late afternoon to swim first and stay for sunset; carry cash as card networks are patchy and ATMs unreliable.
address: Beach No. 7, Radhanagar, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Elephant Beach on the northwest coast of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) is the island's main water-sports hub, reached by a 20-30 minute speedboat ride from Havelock Jetty or a ~2 km forest trek. Its shallow fringing coral reef starts barely 30 metres from the sand, making it the easiest-access snorkeling in the Andamans. Activities on offer include snorkeling, scuba diving, sea walking, parasailing, jet skiing, glass-bottom boat rides and banana boats.
place_tip: Activities run roughly 11 AM to 4 PM; arrive early because you only get about 3 hours on the beach and all activities share the slot.
address: Northwest coast, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Kalapathar Beach on the eastern shore of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) is named for the black rocks (kala pathar) lining its shore, creating a dramatic contrast with the white sand and turquoise water. It is one of the island's best sunrise beaches and is ideal for peaceful morning walks and photography. Swimming is discouraged due to strong currents and rocky patches.
place_tip: Go at sunrise for the best light; avoid swimming here and stick to the shore walk.
address: Eastern shore, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Vijaynagar Beach, known locally as Beach No. 5, is a long stretch of white sand on the east coast of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) near Vijaynagar village. It is quieter than Radhanagar and Elephant Beach, with calm clear water, fringing mahua trees, and good conditions for swimming, beachcombing and bird watching. The beachfront area has some of the island's popular cafes and eateries.
place_tip: Good for a relaxed swim and a meal nearby; combine with a visit to the cafes along Beach No. 5.
address: Beach No. 5, Vijaynagar, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Govind Nagar Beach, locally Beach No. 3, is a long crescent of powder-soft sand on the eastern shoreline of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), fronting the island's main village and its cafes, dive stores and homestays. It has shallow swimmable water year round, a fringe reef with parrotfish and clownfish, and a vivid sunrise; knee-deep ruins of a WWII pier can be seen in the lagoon. This is also where several scuba operators run beginner dives, including at Nemo Reef.
place_tip: Ideal for a sunrise swim or a morning dive; the village market and cheap dhabas are a short walk away.
address: Beach No. 3, Govind Nagar, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Neil's Cove is a small secluded lagoon about 1 km north of Radhanagar Beach on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), reached by a 15-20 minute walk past a rocky corner of the main beach. The lagoon has shallow, transparent water, unusual eroded rock formations and colourful fish, and is known for snorkeling at low tide. Sources advise against swimming at dawn and dusk because saltwater crocodiles have been sighted, and against visiting alone.
place_tip: Visit only at low tide and in daylight, never alone; carry all water and supplies as there are no shops nearby.
address: North end of Radhanagar Beach, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Aquarium is one of Swaraj Dweep's (Havelock Island's) best-known beginner dive sites, a fringing reef about 3 km offshore from Elephant Beach in 6-14 m of water. The reef is dense with hard and soft corals and schooling reef fish — clownfish, parrotfish, moray eels — with occasional reef sharks, in excellent visibility. It is widely used for Discover Scuba Diving (DSD) try-dives and Open Water training.
place_tip: Book with a PADI/SSI-certified dive centre; beginners can do a no-certification Discover Scuba dive with an instructor.
address: Offshore (~3 km from Elephant Beach), Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Scuba diving near Elephant Beach is aimed at first-time and novice divers on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), with shallow shore dives and boat dives over the beach's fringing reef. Certified PADI/SSI centres on the island run Discover Scuba Diving sessions with an instructor for non-swimmers, while experienced divers head to deeper offshore sites like Aquarium and Dickson's Pinnacle. The season runs roughly October to May when visibility is best.
place_tip: You do not need to know swimming for a Discover Scuba dive; book a day ahead in peak season as slots fill.
address: Elephant Beach, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Daytime mangrove kayaking on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) starts near Havelock Jetty and paddles into narrow emerald creeks flanked by dense mangrove roots. Guides point out mudskippers, fiddler crabs and kingfishers, and explain how the mangroves protect the island's coastline. It is beginner-friendly, needs no swimming skill, and life jackets and briefings are provided.
place_tip: Wear quick-dry clothes and bring insect repellent; morning sessions are calmer and cooler.
address: Near Havelock Jetty, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: On dark, moonless nights on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), paddling the sheltered waters near the jetty sets off flashes of blue-green light from plankton (Noctiluca scintillans), leaving glowing trails behind each paddle stroke. Guided pre-dawn tours typically start around 3:00-3:30 AM and end at sunrise, and operators also run evening slots after sunset. The glow is brightest in the calm November-to-February window, near the new moon.
place_tip: Book for a night close to the new moon — moonlight washes out the glow; personal cameras are usually not allowed on night tours.
address: Near Havelock Jetty, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: The alternative, budget way to reach Elephant Beach on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) is a ~2 km trek through coastal forest starting from the trailhead past the Radhanagar road, about 8 km from Havelock Jetty. The easy-moderate walk takes 40-60 minutes each way through tropical greenery and is free; an optional local guide costs a few hundred rupees. The trail can be muddy after rain and may close in monsoon.
place_tip: Wear proper footwear with grip and start early — the trail gets muddy after rain and the final stretch can flood at high tide.
address: Trailhead off Radhanagar road (~8 km from Havelock Jetty), Swaraj Dweep, 744211

ai_summary: Sea walking at Elephant Beach lets visitors walk on the ocean floor in a special helmet that supplies air, watching coral and reef fish up close without any swimming or diving skill. It is one of the fixed-price activities sold at the Elephant Beach counter, alongside snorkeling, parasailing and jet skiing. Traveler reports list the price around Rs 3,200 plus a photo/video charge.
place_tip: Book your activities at the Havelock Jetty ticket counter before boarding — boats allow only about 3 hours on the beach.
address: Elephant Beach, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Parasailing is offered at Elephant Beach as one of its signature paid activities, lifting riders for a high-altitude view over the reef and the turquoise bay. Traveler reports list the price around Rs 3,200 for about 3 minutes of flight, with an optional photo/video charge; operators do not dip riders in the water for safety reasons. It is sold alongside sea walking, snorkeling and jet skiing at the Elephant Beach activity counter.
place_tip: Book early in your 3-hour beach slot and carry cash — some activities at the beach counter sell only on cash.
address: Elephant Beach, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

place_name: Glass-Bottom Boat Ride at Elephant Beach
name_english: Glass-Bottom Boat Ride at Elephant Beach
ai_summary: The glass-bottom boat ride at Elephant Beach lets non-swimmers and families see the shallow coral reef and reef fish through a viewing hull without getting wet. Tickets are sold at the Havelock Jetty or at the Elephant Beach counter alongside other water activities. It is one of the gentler ways to experience the reef, suitable for children and older travelers.
place_tip: Good fallback if the sea is too choppy for snorkeling; book at the jetty counter before boarding.
address: Elephant Beach, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Market No. 3 in Govind Nagar is the main local market of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), with shops selling souvenirs such as sea-shell and wooden jewellery, plus fresh fruit, vegetables and fish. It is also the practical heart of the island with vegetable and fish markets, small shops, cheap dhabas, petrol sellers, banks and ATMs. Several souvenir shops line the main street opposite Beach 2 resorts.
place_tip: Combine with an evening stroll through Govind Nagar village; withdraw cash here as ATMs elsewhere are unreliable.
address: Govind Nagar, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Sagarika Emporium is a government-run handicraft stall inside the Radhanagar Beach premises on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), selling authentic local crafts and souvenirs. Being inside the beach complex, it is a convenient stop for picking up fixed-price local items before or after swimming and the sunset. A larger Sagarika Emporium also operates in Port Blair.
place_tip: Shop here for fixed, government-set prices before bargaining at beachside stalls.
address: Radhanagar Beach premises, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Inglis Island is an uninhabited island about 35 km (1.5-2 hours by boat) from Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), run as a day-trip excursion from Havelock Jetty. Travelers describe it as Havelock's best-kept secret: white-sand beaches, rocky shores and a rock arch, very rich snorkeling with colourful corals and marine life, and a short jungle trail. Trips are seasonal and sea-condition dependent.
place_tip: Go in a group with a registered operator and pack all food and water — there are no facilities on the island.
address: Offshore (~35 km from Havelock Jetty), Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Shaheed Dweep, still widely called Neil Island, lies about 15 km from Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) in Ritchie's Archipelago and makes a popular day trip by inter-island ferry (about 45-60 minutes). The quieter island offers Laxmanpur Beach's famous sunset point, Bharatpur Beach's coral reefs, Sitapur Beach and the natural rock bridge (Howrah Bridge). Travelers often describe it as the slower, more laid-back alternative to Havelock.
place_tip: Book the inter-island ferry in advance in peak season and target Laxmanpur Beach for sunset before the return sailing.
address: Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Ritchie's Archipelago, 744104

place_name: Port Blair Day Trip (Cellular Jail, Ross Island)
name_english: Port Blair Day Trip (Cellular Jail and Ross Island)
ai_summary: Port Blair, officially Sri Vijaya Puram, is about 41 km by sea from Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) and makes a long but rewarding day trip by morning ferry. Highlights include the Cellular Jail (Kaala Paani) national memorial with its evening light-and-sound show, Ross Island's colonial-era ruins and spotted deer, and North Bay's coral reefs. Government and private ferries connect Havelock with Haddo/Phoenix Bay jetties in 1.5-2.5 hours.
place_tip: Take the earliest ferry out and the evening ferry back; book both ferries a day ahead in peak season.
address: Port Blair (Sri Vijaya Puram), South Andaman, 744101

ai_summary: Baratang Island, roughly 100 km by sea-and-road from Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), is a full-day excursion combining a ferry crossing with a drive through the Jarawa tribal reserve forest. The main sights are the limestone caves reached via a mangrove-creek boat ride and the Parrot Island sunset point where thousands of parakeets return at dusk. Trips leave very early in the morning with government convoy timings.
place_tip: This is a dawn-to-dusk trip with reserve convoy rules — go with a registered operator and carry ID.
address: Baratang Island, Middle Andaman, 744201

ai_summary: Something Different is the best-known beachside cafe of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), set directly on Beach No. 2 behind the Havelock Power House with open sea views. It serves Indian, Chinese and Continental dishes with milkshakes and light snacks; signature items include fish fry, crab lollipops, almond pudding and pizzas. Reviewers highlight the warm service, free pickup/drop and personal touches like complimentary framed photos.
place_tip: Reserve ahead for a romantic beach dinner; ask for the free pickup/drop service from nearby hotels.
address: Beach No. 2, behind Havelock Power House, Govind Nagar, Swaraj Dweep, 744211

ai_summary: Anju Coco Resto is a long-running seafood restaurant on Beach No. 5 (Vijaynagar) of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), known for fresh catch dishes served near the water. It is listed among the island's most-reviewed eateries (1,000+ reviews) with seafood, Indian and Chinese items, in the mid price band. The setting is a simple thatched beachside restaurant popular with both tourists and locals.
place_tip: Go for fresh grilled seafood at dinner; evenings are breezy right by the beach.
address: Beach No. 5, Vijaynagar, Swaraj Dweep, 744211

ai_summary: Full Moon Cafe is a much-loved beachside cafe on the Govind Nagar side of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), near Beach No. 3, with an open outdoor seating area facing the sea. It serves Indian, cafe-style and seafood dishes (4.4 rating from 900+ reviews) and is a favourite for long relaxed lunches and evening sessions. Reviewers note friendly staff and generous portions.
place_tip: Good for a long lazy lunch by the sea; evenings fill up, so arrive a bit early.
address: Havelock Beach No. 3, Govind Nagar, Swaraj Dweep, 744211

ai_summary: Golden Spoon is a popular seafood restaurant near Havelock Island Beach Resort on the Govind Nagar beach belt of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island). It is known for grilled fish, including the banana-leaf grilled fish, and serves Indian and seafood dishes in the mid price band. Reviewers describe it as a reliable choice for seafood close to the Govind Nagar resorts.
place_tip: Order the banana-leaf grilled fish if available; it is the dish reviewers praise most.
address: Near Havelock Island Beach Resort, Govind Nagar, Swaraj Dweep, 744211

ai_summary: Squid Restaurant is a simple, home-style Indian restaurant in the Govind Nagar area of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), noted in traveler guides as a budget-friendly local option. It serves curries and stir-fries with a homely touch, and is referenced in island guides as a landmark near the Govind Nagar market/ANIIDCO wine shop area. Good for unpretentious, affordable meals.
place_tip: A good budget lunch stop near the Govind Nagar market; mains are modestly priced for the island.
address: Govind Nagar, Swaraj Dweep, 744211

ai_summary: Famous Seafood Restaurant is the highest-rated restaurant in Swaraj Dweep on Tripadvisor (4.9 from ~200 reviews), an Indian/seafood spot on the Govind Nagar beach belt. Reviewers praise crab masala, butter chicken, golden prawns and grilled whole fish, with friendly owners and staff. It is known for delivery and takeaway service on the island.
place_tip: Try the crab masala or grilled whole fish; ask about delivery if you are staying nearby.
address: Govind Nagar, Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), 744211

ai_summary: Bharatpur Beach is Shaheed Dweep's busiest and most visitor-friendly beach, about 500 metres from the Neil Island jetty on the east side of the island (formerly Neil Island). Its long stretch of white sand and shallow, clear turquoise water is lined with coral reefs, making it the island's main hub for swimming, snorkelling, glass-bottom boat rides and seasonal water sports.
place_tip: Go early morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat and crowds; carry your own water and reef-safe sunscreen.
address: Bharatpur, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: Laxmanpur Beach on the island's west coast is Shaheed Dweep's famous sunset beach, split into Laxmanpur 1 (the main sunset stretch) and Laxmanpur 2 (quieter, and the access point for the Natural Bridge at low tide). Its broad white-sand shoreline, coral fragments and calm evening light make it the most photographed evening spot on the island (formerly Neil Island).
place_tip: Arrive 45-60 minutes before sunset to find a good spot; at high tide stay out of the water as currents can be strong.
address: Laxmanpur, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: Sitapur Beach on the east coast of Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) is known as the island's sunrise beach, facing open sea with views of the rising sun painting the sky in bright colours. Fringed by tropical vegetation and rocky coastal sections, it is a calm, quiet spot suited to early-morning walks and meditation.
place_tip: Arrange transport the previous evening, as taxis and autos are scarce before dawn; reach by 5:15 AM to catch the full sunrise.
address: Sitapur, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: The Natural Bridge, locally nicknamed Howrah Bridge by Bengali settlers, is a natural limestone and living-coral sea arch near Laxmanpur Beach No. 2 on Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island). Reached by a 300-400 m walk over exposed rocky reef, it is accessible only during the day's low-tide window, when tide pools around it reveal sea cucumbers, crabs, brittle stars and giant clams.
place_tip: Check the local tide schedule or ask a local guide before going; wear grippy footwear for the sharp coral path and do not step on living coral.
cost: Free
address: Laxmanpur Beach No. 2, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: Ram Nagar Beach is the quieter, less-visited beach on Shaheed Dweep's (Neil Island's) northern side, valued for its seclusion, clean sand and calm ambience away from the island's main tourist spots. The lagoons near Ram Nagar are also listed among the island's snorkelling areas, and a few beach cafés and dive shops sit along its shore.
place_tip: Best for a peaceful picnic or beach walk; carry everything you need, as facilities are fewer here than at Bharatpur.
address: Ram Nagar, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: Neil Kendra is the central village and market area of Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), where visitors can see daily island life, buy souvenirs, local honey and spices, and eat at small local eateries and sweet shops. Shops here typically open around 9 AM to 6 PM, and the area anchors the island's modest shopping and dining scene.
place_tip: Browse in the late morning when shops are fully open; try Sutapa Sweets in the main market for Indian sweets and samosas.
address: Neil Kendra village, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: The Shaheed Dweep Jetty (Neil Jetty) is the island's ferry gateway, handling government ferries and private cruises (Makruzz, Coastal Cruise, Express Bhagya) to Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) and Swaraj Dweep (Havelock). The long jetty walkway over clear blue water offers marine-life views, and glass-bottom boat rides for coral viewing depart from here.
place_tip: Book ferries in advance during peak season (December-February); arrive early for your sailing as boarding is on foot along the jetty.
address: Shaheed Dweep Jetty, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

place_name: Scuba Diving Sites (K-Rock, Bus Stop, Margherita's Mischief, Jetty Channel Marker)
name_english: Scuba Diving Sites (K-Rock, Bus Stop, Margherita's Mischief, Jetty Channel Marker)
ai_summary: The waters around Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) host several named dive sites listed by the Andaman & Nicobar tourism department: Bus Stop (for beginners and certified divers), Margherita's Mischief (rocky mounds with potential dugong sightings), Jetty Channel Marker (shallow fringing reef for new divers) and K-Rock (schools of fusiliers, trevallies, butterflyfish, Napoleon wrasse, occasional reef sharks and turtles). Local dive shops including Indian Scuba Explorers, Dive India and Scuba Love run guided dives in these clear, calm waters.
place_tip: Book with a certified operator a day ahead; calm, clear water makes this a good island for beginner discover dives too.
address: Offshore dive sites, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: The shallow lagoons off Bharatpur Beach and Laxmanpur Beach on Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) are the island's go-to snorkelling spots, with clear water, coral gardens and colourful reef fish close to shore. Equipment can be rented from resorts and beach operators; several resorts lend out snorkelling gear to guests.
place_tip: Best in calm morning seas; avoid touching or standing on the coral, and check local conditions before entering the water.
address: Bharatpur & Laxmanpur lagoons, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: Glass-bottom boat rides depart from the Shaheed Dweep Jetty (Neil Island) and give non-swimmers and children a dry view of the coral reefs and marine life through a transparent hull. The typical ride runs about 20 minutes and costs roughly INR 400 to INR 600 per person, per published local guides.
place_tip: Pick a morning ride in calm seas for the clearest views through the glass hull.
cost: Rs 400-600 per person
address: Shaheed Dweep Jetty, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) is small - about 13.7 square kilometres - and famously flat, so cycling is the classic way to explore it, with cycle rentals available around Neil Kendra for roughly INR 100-200 per day. A ride across the island passes paddy fields, banana plantations, quiet villages and the roads linking all three main beaches.
place_tip: Start early (by 6-6:30 AM) to combine the ride with a sunrise stop at Sitapur Beach and avoid the midday heat.
cost: Rs 100-200 per day (cycle rental)
address: Neil Kendra, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: With minimal light pollution and open sea horizons, the dark beaches of Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) - especially Laxmanpur and Sitapur - are described by the Andaman & Nicobar tourism department as natural open-air observatories. On clear nights the sky reveals constellations, shooting stars and the Milky Way above swaying palms and gentle waves.
place_tip: Pick a moonless, cloud-free night in the dry season and walk a few minutes away from any resort lights for the darkest sky.
address: Laxmanpur & Sitapur beaches, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

place_name: Farm Walk - Vegetable Bowl of the Andamans
name_english: Farm Walk - Vegetable Bowl of the Andamans
ai_summary: Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) is nicknamed the 'Vegetable Bowl of the Andamans' for its flat, fertile farmland, and guided walks through its paddy fields, banana plantations and village lanes are a standard local experience. The walks show a slower, agricultural side of island life that sets Neil apart from the more resort-driven islands.
place_tip: Take a guided walk so you don't get lost in the field tracks; combine it with a cycle ride through the village lanes.
address: Village farmlands, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: Bharatpur Beach is Shaheed Dweep's (Neil Island's) main water-sports hub, where seasonal operators offer jet skiing, banana boat rides and speed boating over the shallow turquoise lagoon, subject to weather, tides and local permissions. It is the liveliest beach on the island and the easiest place to try motorised water sports without leaving the island.
place_tip: Confirm the day's availability and price with the operator on the beach before paying; rides depend on sea and weather conditions.
address: Bharatpur Beach, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

place_name: Radhanagar Beach, Swaraj Dweep (~17 km by sea)
name_english: Radhanagar Beach, Swaraj Dweep (~17 km by sea)
ai_summary: DAY TRIP: Radhanagar Beach on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) is about 17 km by sea from Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) - roughly an hour by ferry - and was named Asia's best beach by Time magazine in 2004. Its 2-km stretch of fine white sand, turquoise water and jungle fringe, about 12 km from Havelock's ferry pier, makes it the Andamans' most celebrated sunset beach.
place_tip: Take an early ferry so you can spend the afternoon here and still catch a return sailing; carry essentials as the beach has limited shops.
address: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744211

place_name: Elephant Beach, Swaraj Dweep (~25-30 km by sea)
name_english: Elephant Beach, Swaraj Dweep (~25-30 km by sea)
ai_summary: DAY TRIP: Elephant Beach on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) - about 6 km by sea from the Havelock jetty, reached by a ~45-minute boat ride - is known for some of the Andamans' best coral reefs and lively underwater marine life. Operators run snorkelling, scuba diving, sea walk, jet skiing and parasailing here on a spot-payment basis, making it the archipelago's main adventure-water-sports beach.
place_tip: Carry lunch, drinking water and a change of clothes, as suggested by tour operators; book the boat a day ahead in peak season.
address: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744211

place_name: Kalapathar Beach, Swaraj Dweep (~20 km by sea)
name_english: Kalapathar Beach, Swaraj Dweep (~20 km by sea)
ai_summary: DAY TRIP: Kalapathar Beach on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) is a sunrise beach of black rocks, white sand and turquoise water, best visited in the early morning before the heat builds. It is a quieter alternative to Radhanagar, typically visited for sunrise views and beach walks on Andaman itineraries combining Havelock and Neil Island.
place_tip: Go for sunrise; combine with Radhanagar and Elephant Beach into a full Havelock day if ferry timings allow.
address: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744211

place_name: Cellular Jail & Sound & Light Show, Sri Vijaya Puram (~40 km)
name_english: Cellular Jail & Sound & Light Show, Sri Vijaya Puram (~40 km)
ai_summary: DAY TRIP: The Cellular Jail (Kala Pani) in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) - about 36-40 km and 1.5-2 hours by ferry from Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) - is the three-storeyed colonial prison built in 1906 that held Indian freedom fighters. Its evening Sound & Light Show brings the saga of the freedom struggle alive and is the centrepiece of most Port Blair visits.
place_tip: The Sound & Light Show runs in the evening, so plan a full day: early ferry out, city sights, show at dusk, late ferry back.
address: Atlanta Point, Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

place_name: Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep), Sri Vijaya Puram (~40 km)
name_english: Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep), Sri Vijaya Puram (~40 km)
ai_summary: DAY TRIP: Ross Island (renamed Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep) near Sri Vijaya Puram - about 40 km by ferry from Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) - was the British administrative headquarters, nicknamed the 'Paris of the East', now lying in ruins after earthquakes. Visitors walk among crumbling colonial buildings alongside deer and peacocks, then combine the trip with nearby North Bay (Coral Island) for snorkelling.
place_tip: Combine with a North Bay coral-viewing boat trip in the same harbour cruise day; carry sun protection and water.
address: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman & Nicobar 744102

place_name: Corbyn's Cove Beach, Sri Vijaya Puram (~40 km)
name_english: Corbyn's Cove Beach, Sri Vijaya Puram (~40 km)
ai_summary: DAY TRIP: Corbyn's Cove Beach, about 7 km from Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) - roughly 40 km by ferry from Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) - is a coconut-palm-fringed beach suited to swimming, sunbathing and water sports. It is the standard beach stop on Port Blair city tours and pairs well with the Cellular Jail visit on the same day.
place_tip: Combine with the Cellular Jail and museums on a single Port Blair day trip to make the 1.5-2 hour ferry worthwhile.
address: Corbyn's Cove, Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: Avisa is a pet-friendly beach café behind the ScubaYogi dive shop at Ram Nagar Beach on Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), open since 2023 and ranked #2 of 21 island restaurants on TripAdvisor with a 5-star rating. Its menu spans Italian, Indian, seafood, pizza, Mediterranean and café dishes (price range about Rs 169-2,500), and reviewers highlight fresh seafood, the laid-back beachfront pavilion and sunset views.
place_tip: Head here for sunset dinner; the open-air pavilion is about 50 metres from the beach and fills up in peak season.
address: Behind ScubaYogi Dive Shop, Ram Nagar Beach, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: Garden View Restaurant near the Shaheed Dweep Jetty on Neil Island is a well-known casual eatery famous for its grilled fish, a favourite stop for visitors right after landing. It serves conventional Indian and seafood preparations at budget-friendly prices in a simple, family-run setting.
place_tip: Convenient first meal after the ferry; ask for the day's fresh catch grilled.
address: Near Shaheed Dweep Jetty, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: Dugong by SeaShell is the restaurant at SeaShell Resorts on Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), noted for its premium dine-in experience, beachfront setting and a wide selection of Indian, Continental and seafood dishes. Reviewers call out the seafood platter, Neil fish curry, chilli chicken and crispy chilli baby corn as standout orders.
place_tip: Reserve ahead for a beachfront dinner table; it is the island's most upscale dinner option.
address: SeaShell, Beach No 1, Village Road, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: Blue Sea Restaurant at Laxmanpur Beach on Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) is known for its creamy coconut prawn curry and other fresh seafood preparations. It is a convenient sunset-time dinner stop for visitors spending the evening on the island's sunset beach.
place_tip: Time your meal with the Laxmanpur sunset; order the coconut prawn curry if available.
address: Laxmanpur Beach, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: Gan Garden Restaurant, about 500 metres from the main bazaar on the road towards the sunset point on Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), is a family-run restaurant opposite the football ground with a good choice of meals. The family will happily cook fish you catch or buy from the fish market for a small charge, and also helps arrange snorkelling, fishing and jungle trips.
place_tip: If you fish or buy from the market, ask the family to cook it; ask about their snorkelling and fishing day trips (about Rs 500 per person, full day with lunch).
address: About 500 m from Neil Kendra bazaar towards Laxmanpur, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104

ai_summary: OrganiKa in Ram Nagar on Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) is the island's noted vegetarian option, serving a veg thali of local vegetable dishes with rice and chapati made from fresh local produce. It is a useful stop for vegetarian travellers on an island where most eateries lead with seafood.
place_tip: The island's reliable vegetarian bet; the veg thali showcases the local 'vegetable bowl' produce.
address: Ram Nagar, Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island), Andaman & Nicobar 744104
